88.t: Battle of the bands at the Apex: Buck Clayton versus Les Hite
88.s: He recalls Buck Clayton's Fourteen Gentlemen of Harlem facing Les Hite's Cotton Club band, listing Hite's sidemen, and Clayton's band being stranded in China.
88.ch: Early Los Angeles and first bands
88.q: Okay. It seems to me right about this time was when Buck Clayton had formed a band called The Fourteen Gentlemen of Harlem, and Les Hylte was at the Cotton Club, and he had a drummer which was Lionel Hampton, which was with Les Hylte. But Buck Clayton had a drummer -- I got it -- his name was Baby…

88.s: Eddie Barefield stayed in Los Angeles and formed a band with Paul Howard, Jack McVea and Dudley Brooks that rehearsed with new arrangements daily.
88.ch: Fats Waller, Nat Cole and Les Hite
88.q: Well, in later years, he went -- no, we called him Papoose out here, that's what it was; that's what the story is -- he was Indian and he was rehearsing with Barefield's band also, and in later years when we saw him back east -- he went back east and started to play with all the bands, but out here…

88.t: Early Los Angeles bandleaders: Irving Brothers, Rebb Spikes, Earl Dancer, Edith Turnham
88.s: Lee responds to Chilton's names of early thirties Los Angeles bands and adds Edith Turnham, whose son Floyd played lead alto.
88.q: Yeah, there were some Irving Brothers, but ... yeah, they were early, though. Yeah, they were. It seems like one played guitar and another one played bad piano. I think ... I don't know. But yeah, I remember the names -- but I think this was a little bit before I got out there.

18.t: Benny Morton and Claude Jones in Henderson's band
18.s: Henderson had Jones and Morton; he let Jones go and JCH and Morton worked together.
18.ch: Family lore, Boston and Europe with Sam Price
18.q: He had two trombones. He had Claude Jones and Benny Morton... He let Claude go and Benny and I worked together.

18.s: He and Allen kept moving between Mills' Blue Rhythm Band, Lucky Millinder and Fletcher Henderson.
18.ch: Cincinnati, Buffalo, Russell and Fletcher Henderson
18.q: : Mills' Blue Rhythm Band. When I was with Lucky's band we were in Philadelphia and I got a telegram from Fletcher Henderson, asking me to call him. I've got it in the scrapbook. He said, "I want to talk to you about Red Allen." That's when Red and I went with Fletcher. We'd switch around like that.

18.t: How long he stayed with Henderson
18.s: He stayed two to four years, then went to the Russell band after Armstrong took it over.
18.ch: Cincinnati, Buffalo, Russell and Fletcher Henderson
18.q: : With Fletcher? I've got the whole album of that. John Hammond gave it to me, the whole album.

28.t: Horace Henderson's band; the 1933 Berlin summer contract
28.s: Returning in 1929 after Fowler and Roberts, Butler joined Horace Henderson's band, playing his brother's music at college proms and parties at the Dunbar Palace until about 1933-34. He then took a summer contract at the Feminina in Berlin in 1933.
28.ch: Lucky Roberts, Armstrong and the big-band rivalries
28.q: No, I went with Billy Fowler's band, I had come back in '29. Now Horace Henderson, Fletcher Henderson's brother, he assembled a band. And so I got in that band.

28.t: The Lenox Club band under Cliff Jackson and Jeff Blunt
28.s: The Lenox Club drew number runners and the Cotton Club's turned-away crowd; the ten-piece band played hard syncopated numbers, with Herb Branch and Edgar Allen on lead trumpet.
28.ch: Newark and first years in Harlem
28.q: And he had one of those heads on him. But now this Lenox Club, it was where the people who wanted to be like -- they had the same bandstand, somewhat, we had a 10-piece band, Cliff Jackson was the band leader. And he had a sock cymbal on his foot. It seems as though the rhythm wasn't moving him or…

91.t: Subbing for Don Redman in Fletcher Henderson's band
91.s: Playing at the Cameo Club with Billy Fowler, he was asked to sub for Don Redman at Roseland, with Fowler's blessing.
91.q: And Fletcher was playing at Roseland. Don Redman -- if I'm correct about this -- I think that Don Redman's father, or someone in the family passed, and Don had to go to Piedmont,West Virginia, which I think was his hometown, and he was going to be gone a week or two, and Fletcher asked me if I…

91.t: Replacing Don Redman at Henderson and McKinney's Cotton Pickers
91.s: He replaced Redman with Fletcher and later with McKinney's, having recorded with them earlier; the arranging parallels were coincidence.
91.q: Yes, I did, because then when Don finally went with McKinney's Cottonpickers, Fletcher invited me in to the band to replace Don.

473.t: Horace Henderson's trumpet section: Red Holland, Bernice Morton and Roy
473.s: The band's trumpets were Roy, Bernice Morton (Spratt) and Matthew 'Red' Holland, all but Roy from the Louisville kid band; when Red left, Jones took his place, his second professional job.
473.ch: Riverboat to New Orleans and Horace Henderson
473.q: And he was -- well, he's deceased now, but he was a nice little trumpet player. He was out of the band. There was a whole trumpet section, all but Roy -- they had Red Holland on trumpet. I spoke about him before. Matthew Holland was his name. And he left --

473.t: Back to Stuff's bigger Vendome band on a steady job
473.s: Dance interrupts to untangle the chronology; Jones and Stuff got along well and the Vendome job was steady, until Jimmy Smith's invitation to New York came.
473.ch: Buffalo, Lunceford, Lil Armstrong and Stuff Smith
473.q: Now I got away from Stuff -- oh, yeah, now I've got to go back to when about '32, in the middle of that, things are happening in there, you know, with Stuff awhile and Lunceford awhile, and they sent for me to come down to -- Jimmy Smith was his name, a bass player, out of the Missourians. He…

178.s: Ferbos worked on and off with Bigfoot Bill's small band, including Maurice Justin and Hippolyte Francis.
178.q: He did a big band or something? Yeah. He did a big band or something? Yeah. He did a big band or something? Yeah. He did a big band or something? Yeah. Yeah. One time he had a big band but most of the time we had about five pieces I think we used to work.

41.t: Paul's 1934 band at Harry's New Yorker and the OK recording
41.s: Mares explains the 1934 personnel and that Omer Simeon replaced Fazola on a four-side recording date.
41.q: Yes, he got the date for Paul to record four sides. And Fazola was supposed to play with Paul's outfit and he just couldn't make it. And the date was scheduled for that day and they used Omer Simeon at that time.

193.t: First job with Kid Thomas and other names
193.s: His first job was with Kid Thomas, with whom he has played about 39 years; he mentions Fletcher Henderson, Red Allen and his nicknames.
193.q: That's my first job. He's a famous band. He's been playing about, I guess, about 50 years. I've been playing with him about 39 years myself.

573.t: Pensacola band, Edmond Hall, and when Sam joined
573.s: Clarifying the Pensacola band and its players, and when Sam came into the band, around 1932-33.
573.q: I don't know. I think Lee was playing with them, if I'm mistaken. I don't know who was the trumpet player, but I know Mack wasn't playing with them.

323.t: Joining Paul Whiteman: hotels, Woodbury radio show and the sax section
323.s: Joining Whiteman in spring 1936, Billy Rose's Jumbo, Adolph Deutsch, and the five-man sax section.
323.q: Oh well with the Whiteman band hotel rooms were so reasonable. We used to get a rate. $2.50 single. Not the Waldorf, but good hotels. No flea bags. Like Goldie used to say, no flea bags you know. And it was great traveling with the band, the Whiteman band. And I’ll never forget. See I joined spring…

109.t: Black Cat musicians scatter; he joins Edgar Hayes
109.s: After almost a year at the Black Cat, with Freddie Green, Bobby Moore and Frank Clarke gone, Clarke joined Edgar Hayes late in 1936.
109.q: Freddie joined Basie, and after, as Atkins, the a piano player, he went back to Philadelphia, and Lonny went to Chicago to play organ.

80.t: Dating his joining Fats, and taking Claude Hopkins dates while Fats was idle
80.s: He started moving with Fats in 1934; when Fats was in town with nothing happening, he got Fats's permission to play West Virginia dates with Claude Hopkins.
80.ch: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
80.q: Same thing, hang around and, you know, work wherever I could. Grab club dates, or whatnot, you know, and there wasn't a hell of a lot then, for me, as a colored guy, I'll put it that way. They -- well, there weren't too many colored club dates, anyway.

145.t: McKinney's Cotton Pickers arrive; Royal joins Les Hite at Sebastian's
145.s: Royal admires McKinney's Cotton Pickers under Don Redman, and Les Hite, needing another saxophonist, calls him down from San Francisco, reuniting him with Lawrence Brown.
145.ch: Les Hite, Sebastian's and Duke Ellington
145.q: Oh, I worked with them about a year or so. Then a band by the name of McKinney's Cotton Pickers came to town and they went to work at Sebastian's Cotton Club. By far, they had one of the best bands that I had ever heard in my life. I think of all the bands at that time, there were only two that I…

87.t: Leaving Tommy Miles for Earl Hines; Tyree Glenn and Eckstine
87.s: Mundy went to Hines first and brought Young; Tyree Glenn replaced him in Miles's band, and Eckstine sang regularly only after.
87.ch: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
87.q: Yeah, because Jimmy Mundy went first, and he told Earl about us. He said I can get some guys can really help your band. So, I was one of the guys that came over. And this is before Billy -- I knew Eckstine before he came with Tommy too. He came a little later. He was with Tommy when Tyree was with…

17.t: Edgar Battle: hiring him for Blanche and composing 'Topsy'
17.ch: Opinions, Edgar Battle and closing stories
17.q: Well Edgar Battle is, I finished telling you a little while ago that he was a very dear friend. Edgar Battle I've been knowing him, he is the one that recruited me out of New York to go with Blanche Calloway.

146.t: Recruiting Hot Lips Page from Sugar Lou and Eddie
146.s: The band heard of Hot Lips Page in a seven-piece band and he joined because the Blue Devils worked more.
146.q: : Yeah. That was his home, in Corsicana. But he was in a little band down there called Sugar Lou and Eddie. That's the band he was with. He had a little seven-piece band there. So we heard about it. So we ran into him... We ran into him somewhere. Anyway, he got the wind that we wanted him. So he…

89.t: Organizing Fletcher Henderson's first band for Ethel Waters
89.s: He helped organize Fletcher's eight-piece band that toured with Ethel Waters; Fletcher then hired Coleman Hawkins and moved to the Club Alabam.
89.ch: Fletcher, Wooding and the Harlem scene
89.q: Oh, let me tell you -- you see something we've omitted in '22, latter part -- or the middle of '22 -- organizing Fletcher Henderson's group for Ethel Waters. That was the next blues singer after Mamie.

758.s: Having saved $500, Roy gambled it away in Philadelphia and then joined Fletcher, where Chu Berry had recommended him; the trumpet section included Thigpen.
758.q: : Yeah, Fletcher asked me to go with him, and I had saved up about five hundred dollars, and I just figured... I told Fletcher I had to go home, but I didn't get no farther than Philadelphia. I went over there with the five hundred dollars and got stranded, you know, with gambling, and I'd take all…

70.t: Leaving McKinney in 1932 and the personnel shuffle
70.s: He stayed until about May 1932; Redman left to form his own band, Carter took over, and Rex Stewart, Hilton Jefferson and others came and went.
70.q: Well, I stayed with that band from December 7, 1930, to about May 1932. And there was a little discrepancy in the band then. Don had left the band and Bennie Carter came but Bennie wasn't that interested in the band either. So Bennie did some writing and all that. So Rex Stewart had come with the…

412.t: Bob Scobey calls him to Chicago in 1959
412.s: Hodes recalls Scobey phoning him in 1959 to replace Tut Soper. He joined for a few days.
412.q: And then work, whatever I could and then what saved me was in 1959, Bob Scobey came to town and called me. Now, I had bad recollections of Scobey from the Lou Waters band. So when he called me, I was visiting my daughter. And I says, no, I don't read that good to read your charts. I'm not…

74.t: Later stint with Fletcher Henderson on college dates
74.s: Mosley later joins Fletcher Henderson for New England college dates; Driggs works out when and says he will check details.
74.ch: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
74.q: Oh yeah, I played Harvard, Yale, Dartmouth and I'll never forget I had that llama coat you saw in that bus and we got up into New Hampshire, somewhere up there, the snow was so heavy, the bus couldn't move. I was with Fletcher.

6.t: Joining Fletcher Henderson in the Big Trade
6.s: In the winter of 1930-31 he went straight from Webb to Henderson, a swap he calls the Big Trade of Carter and Jimmy Harrison for himself and Benny Morton; he also recalls meeting Don Redman.
6.q: Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. It was '31. The winter of '30-'31. I don't remember whether it was after Christmas or before Christmas, but it was the winter.

75.t: Joining Rex Stewart at the Empire Ballroom, 1933
75.s: He joined Rex Stewart in summer 1933, perhaps recommended by U.S. Scott, and recalls the Horace Henderson house band with Sandy Williams and others at the Dunbar.
75.ch: Early 1930s: Bessie Smith, Rex Stewart and the Harlem scene
75.q: I don't know. That's a good question. I do know... U.S. Scott. He was an alto player, a good buddy of mine, we went to school together. Possibly he was the one who recommended me. Maybe that's... I just don't remember how it...

238.s: She lists the Club Alabam band, C. L. Burke, Les Hite, Lloyd Reese and George Orendorff as the local bands when she arrived.
238.ch: Los Angeles scene in the 1930s and 40s
238.q: Well, the one person I remember -- I mean there were several. Lorenzo Flenoy, for instance, was at the Club Alabam. I think I mentioned this earlier. He was at the Club Alabam and he had about a 12 or 13 piece band. Some of the guys that were with him are still around. Lorenzo's passed on since…

13.t: How Earl Hines heard him and five men joined at once
13.s: Hines heard him at the Regal; Wilson, Simeon, Howard, Bishop and Taylor all joined together.
13.ch: Joining Earl Hines and the Grand Terrace
13.q: Well, I guess it was when I was with Dave Peyton. At the Regal. He heard me play, and after Dave Peyton left, then Jerome Carrington took over the band.

79.t: Sorting out the sequence of Henderson, Waller and Tapp
79.s: Tape 2 opens. Dance's reference book gives a different chronology, but Thomas insists he joined Henderson in 1934, then Waller, then Tapp, then Henderson again in 1935. Henderson used scouts and Keg Johnson recommended him.
79.q: No, no. That sequence isn't quite right. He may be on the right track a little more/... than I am. What I did comes into Charlie Turner to Henderson. See, Henderson was the type of fellow who had scouts out.
